intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do for eco-adventurers seeking an adrenaline rush above the treetops.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari spotting howler monkeys, caimans, river otters, toucans, and nesting sea turtles. This remote Caribbean-side park is one of Central America's most biodiverse wildlife corridors.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges suspended up to 100 feet above the forest floor, offering eye-level encounters with sloths, poison dart frogs, and exotic birds against the dramatic backdrop of Arenal Volcano.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Wildlife Guided Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Explore Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal camouflaged sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, and rare birds hidden in the lush coastal rainforest, ending at a pristine white-sand beach.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a guided day hike through Corcovado, home to tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and four species of monkeys. National Geographic called this 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.'

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange a pre-booked shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: shared shuttles cost ~$15–25 vs $80+ for private taxis). Check in, freshen up, and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport — look for a Soda (local Costa Rican diner) inside the terminal for a casado (rice, beans, protein) for ~$6–8, or pick up snacks at a convenience store for the ride

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Exchange a small amount of currency (colones) at the airport for incidentals. Save big exchanges for local banks or ATMs in town for better rates. Store valuables securely. Rest is the priority tonight — big adventures start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a morning stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Watch for coastal birds including frigatebirds, pelicans, and herons. Grab breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town or village on foot. Visit the nearest mercado (market) to pick up fresh tropical fruits — mangoes, papayas, and pineapples — for cheap, healthy snacks throughout the trip. Rent a bicycle (~$10/day) if available locally and cycle along coastal paths. Look for free or low-cost wildlife spotting: iguanas and howler monkeys are often visible near beachside vegetation.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the beach for sunset — Costa Rica sunsets are spectacular and completely free. Find a local soda or beachside restaurant for dinner. Chat with locals and fellow travelers to get insider tips on free wildlife spots and cheap activities in the area.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans with egg) at a local soda — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the market + a casado plate at a local soda — ~$5–7
meals.dinner: Arroz con pollo or fish tacos at a beachside soda — ~$6–9

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is your orientation day. Download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline), buy a local SIM card (~$10–15 with data), and plan your week's activities. Ask hotel staff about free wildlife trails and budget tour operators. February is dry season — expect sunny, warm weather perfect for outdoor adventures.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:30–6:00 AM) for a guided wildlife walk or self-guided nature trail near the resort. February is peak dry season, making it ideal for spotting wildlife at dawn. Look for howler monkeys, white-faced capuchins, sloths hanging in cecropia trees, and colorful toucans. Bring binoculars if you have them — many hostels/hotels lend them for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife reserve. Depending on your coastal location, options may include Manuel Antonio, Tortuguero area trails, or Carara National Park. Entry fees range from $8–18 for foreigners. Explore marked trails independently (no guide fee needed) and keep eyes peeled for scarlet macaws, coatis, and basilisk lizards.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Visit a local pulpería (corner store) to stock up on snacks and drinks. Enjoy the evening on the beach or resort terrace, listening to the sounds of the jungle. Review tomorrow's zip-lining plans.

meals.breakfast: Early gallo pinto and coffee at the hotel or a nearby soda — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch: bread, local cheese, fruit, and juice from the market — ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Casado with fresh fish at a local soda — ~$7–10

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored, lightweight clothing for wildlife watching — avoid bright colors. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, and a reusable water bottle. Early morning is the absolute best time for wildlife activity. Silence is golden on trails — speak softly and move slowly for the best sightings.

day_by_day.morning: ZIP-LINING DAY! Book a budget zip-line tour through a local operator (avoid resort-booked tours which add markup). Look for operators offering 8–12 line courses for $45–65 per person. Depart early to beat the heat. Most zip-line tours include safety briefings, equipment, and guides. Enjoy the adrenaline rush of soaring through the forest canopy with incredible views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, many operators include a short hanging bridges or nature walk component — take full advantage of this. Alternatively, visit a nearby waterfall (many are free or charge a small ~$2–5 entrance fee). Cool off with a swim in a natural pool at the waterfall base.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your zip-line adventure! Head to a local bar or restaurant for a cold Imperial or Pilsen beer (Costa Rica's local brews, ~$2–3 each). Share stories with fellow travelers. Try a traditional Chifrijo (rice, beans, pork rinds, and pico de gallo) as a bar snack.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel — gallo pinto and fresh juice — ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Many zip-line tours include a basic lunch; if not, grab a bocadillo (sandwich) or empanadas from a local vendor — ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Chifrijo and beers at a local bar, or a full casado dinner at a soda — ~$8–12

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining at least 1–2 days in advance, especially in peak February season. Wear closed-toe shoes (mandatory), comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dirty, and secure any loose items. Leave valuables at the hotel. GoPro or action cameras are usually allowed — check with your operator. Tip your guides if service was excellent (~$5 per guide is appreciated).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the zip-line excitement. Sleep in, then take a gentle yoga session on the beach (many resorts offer free or low-cost morning yoga). Alternatively, go for a peaceful early morning swim in the ocean. Practice spotting coastal wildlife: pelicans diving for fish, hermit crabs, and sandpipers along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or colectivo to a nearby town or village (~$1–3 for bus fare). Explore the local culture, visit a handicraft market for souvenirs (bargain respectfully), and pop into a local grocery store (SuperMas, Buen Precio, or Walmart-owned Más x Menos) to stock up on budget supplies: instant coffee, snacks, bottled water, and fruit.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal if your accommodation has kitchen access, or eat at a local soda. Spend the evening planning the second half of your trip. Research free wildlife areas, budget tour operators, and transportation options for upcoming days.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit plate at a beachside café — ~$4–7
meals.lunch: Explore the local town's sodas — try a full casado with your choice of protein for ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal with groceries (pasta, local vegetables, eggs) — ~$3–5, OR soda dinner ~$6–9

day_by_day.notes: February 19 is a good day to book any remaining tours for the second week. Look for combo deals — some operators bundle zip-lining, ATV tours, and wildlife walks for significant savings. Check Facebook groups like 'Budget Travel Costa Rica' for current deals and recommendations from other travelers.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife boat tour or kayak excursion through mangroves (if available near your coastal location). Mangrove ecosystems are incredibly rich in wildlife — expect to see crocodiles, caimans, river otters, roseate spoonbills, and dozens of bird species. Budget boat tours run ~$25–45 per person; kayak rentals ~$15–25.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local crocodile bridge or river viewpoint (often free). The Tarcoles River bridge near Carara is famous for its massive American crocodiles visible from above — completely free to view! Spend the afternoon relaxing at the beach, snorkeling (rent gear for ~$10–15), or exploring tide pools at low tide for marine wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by dinner at a beachfront restaurant. Splurge slightly tonight on fresh whole grilled fish (pargo or corvina) — a Costa Rican specialty worth every colón.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast before the early tour — banana and peanut butter sandwich + coffee from a thermos — ~$2–3
meals.lunch: Beachside ceviche from a local vendor (fresh fish, lime, cilantro) — ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Grilled whole fish with rice, beans, and patacones (fried plantains) at a beachfront restaurant — ~$10–15

day_by_day.notes: For mangrove tours, wear long sleeves and apply insect repellent generously — mosquitoes can be active in mangrove areas even in dry season. Bring a dry bag for your phone and camera. The crocodile bridge at Tarcoles is a free highlight — do not lean over the railing or attempt to feed the crocodiles. Keep a safe distance at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip day trip! Take a shared shuttle or public bus to a nearby national park or eco-destination (Monteverde Cloud Forest, Manuel Antonio, Arenal, or Corcovado depending on your base location). Depart by 6:00–7:00 AM to maximize your time. Public buses are the most budget-friendly option (~$5–15 depending on distance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore your day-trip destination. If visiting Manuel Antonio: hike the park trails (entry ~$18), swim at the famous beach inside the park, and spot squirrel monkeys, sloths, and raccoons. If visiting Monteverde: walk the cloud forest trails, spot resplendent quetzals (February is a good month!), and visit the butterfly and hummingbird gardens (~$15–20).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by shared shuttle or bus. Arrive tired but exhilarated. Grab a simple dinner close to the hotel and review your photos from the day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure — gallo pinto and coffee — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for the day trip to save money: sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and water — ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Simple soda dinner near the hotel upon return — casado or soup — ~$6–8

day_by_day.notes: This is your longest and most ambitious day — prepare the night before. Charge all devices, pack your daypack with: sunscreen, insect repellent, rain jacket (cloud forest can be misty), water (2L minimum), snacks, camera, and cash. Book your return shuttle in advance. Wear sturdy walking shoes. If visiting Manuel Antonio, arrive at park opening (7:00 AM) to beat crowds and see the most wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest morning after the big day trip. Sleep in until 8:00–9:00 AM. Enjoy a slow breakfast and journaling or reading on the beach. Take a gentle swim or beach walk to stretch your legs after yesterday's hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local eco-adventure options near the resort. Look for a canopy walk or hanging bridges experience (different from zip-lining — slower and more focused on wildlife observation). These typically cost $20–35 and offer incredible perspectives of the forest. Alternatively, visit a local butterfly farm or reptile sanctuary (~$10–15 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event if available locally — check with hotel staff about local festivals, markets, or music events. Costa Ricans (Ticos) are warm and welcoming; engage with locals at a neighborhood soda or bar for authentic cultural exchange.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast — pancakes with local honey and fresh fruit at a café — ~$5–8
meals.lunch: Lunch at the butterfly farm or local soda near your afternoon activity — ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Traditional Olla de Carne (beef and vegetable stew) at a local soda — ~$7–10

day_by_day.notes: Day 8 is a good time to do laundry (many budget accommodations have laundry service for ~$5–8 per load, or hand-wash items). Review your remaining budget and adjust spending for the final days. Consider purchasing any remaining souvenirs today while you have time to compare prices rather than rushing at the end of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Second zip-line experience OR try a different eco-adventure: ATV tour through jungle trails (~$60–80), white-water rafting on a nearby river (~$45–75 for Class II–III rapids, great for beginners), or a horseback riding tour through rainforest and beach (~$35–55). Book the activity that most excites you!
day_by_day.afternoon: If you did a morning activity, spend the afternoon at the beach relaxing and swimming. Try bodyboarding — many beach vendors rent boards for ~$5–10/hour. Look for free tide pool exploration at low tide: starfish, sea urchins, and small fish are often visible.
day_by_day.evening: Happy hour at a beachside bar (many offer 2-for-1 drinks from 4:00–6:00 PM). Watch the sunset with a tropical cocktail (try a guaro sour — Costa Rica's national spirit) and meet fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Energy-packed breakfast before the morning activity — eggs, gallo pinto, and coffee — ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Beachside vendor food — fresh coconut water (~$2), fruit skewers, or grilled corn — ~$4–7
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a casual beachside restaurant for a change of pace — ~$8–12

day_by_day.notes: For white-water rafting, no prior experience is needed for Class II–III rivers. Operators provide all equipment including helmets, life jackets, and paddles. Wear a swimsuit under quick-dry clothes. GoPro cameras are usually available to rent from operators for ~$15–20 if you want footage. Secure booking by Day 7 or 8 for best availability.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wildlife photography morning. Wake up at dawn (5:00–5:30 AM) and position yourself near forest edges, rivers, or fruit trees near the resort. This is the golden hour for wildlife activity. Target species: sloths (check cecropia trees), toucans, scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, and poison dart frogs (look on the forest floor near leaf litter). Bring your best camera setup.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project (many offer free or low-cost tours and welcome visitors). Learn about Costa Rica's agricultural heritage — cacao, coffee, and tropical fruit farming. Some farms offer free tastings of fresh cacao or coffee. This is a wonderful, authentic, and budget-friendly experience.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or food experience: some local families and small restaurants offer cooking classes where you learn to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto, ceviche, and tres leches cake (~$20–35 per person, often includes dinner). Book through your hotel or local tourism office.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go breakfast before dawn wildlife walk — banana, granola bar, and thermos coffee — ~$2–3
meals.lunch: Farm tour lunch or local soda — ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner (included in class fee) OR traditional Tico home-style meal at a local soda — ~$7–10

day_by_day.notes: For dawn wildlife walks, silence is absolutely essential. Turn your phone to silent mode and avoid flashlights (use red-light mode if needed — less disruptive to animals). Move in single file and stop frequently to listen. Howler monkeys are often heard before they are seen — their roar carries up to 3 miles through the forest. This is one of the most magical free experiences Costa Rica offers.

day_by_day.morning: Beach and ocean morning. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) — rentals typically cost ~$15–20/hour and many beaches offer free lessons with rental. Alternatively, take a surf lesson if your beach has surfable waves (~$35–50 for a 2-hour group lesson including board and wetsuit). Costa Rica is one of the world's best beginner surf destinations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby waterfall hike. Many waterfalls near coastal areas are reachable by a 1–3 hour hike through secondary forest. Entry fees are usually $5–10 or free. Swim in the cool freshwater pool beneath the falls — a refreshing and beautiful experience. Keep eyes open for wildlife along the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Final souvenir shopping at a local artisan market. Look for handmade items: painted wooden toucans, locally produced coffee (excellent quality and great gifts), hammocks, and Boruca indigenous masks. Bargain politely. Spend the evening packing any purchased items and reviewing your remaining days.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie and toast at a beachside café — ~$4–7
meals.lunch: Picnic at the waterfall — packed sandwiches and fruit from the market — ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Seafood platter at a mid-range local restaurant — splurge slightly for this penultimate full day — ~$12–18

day_by_day.notes: For waterfall hikes, wear water shoes or sturdy sandals with grip — rocks near waterfalls are extremely slippery. Never jump from waterfall heights unless local guides confirm it is safe. Bring a dry bag for electronics. February dry season means waterfalls may have slightly lower flow than wet season, but trails will be much easier and safer to navigate.

day_by_day.morning: Final eco-adventure activity: book a guided bird-watching tour with a local naturalist guide (~$25–45 for a 2–3 hour tour). Costa Rica has over 900 bird species — February is excellent for bird-watching as many species are in breeding plumage. Target species: resplendent quetzal, scarlet macaw, keel-billed toucan, and various hummingbirds. Local guides know exactly where to find them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Slow afternoon — revisit your favorite beach spot, take a final swim, and soak in the last full day of tropical paradise. Write postcards to send home (the Costa Rican postal system — Correos de Costa Rica — is reliable). Reflect on your adventures and favorite memories.
day_by_day.evening: FAREWELL DINNER — treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate an incredible 12-day adventure. Find a restaurant with ocean views and order fresh ceviche, grilled lobster or shrimp (if budget allows), and a tropical dessert like tres leches or churros with dulce de leche. Toast to pura vida!

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and Costa Rican coffee — ~$5–8
meals.lunch: Light lunch — fresh coconut water and ceviche from a beach vendor — ~$6–9
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a nicer local seafood restaurant — budget ~$18–25 for a special meal

day_by_day.notes: Pura vida — the Costa Rican philosophy of pure life, simplicity, and gratitude — is the perfect mindset for your final full day. Tip generously at your farewell dinner (10–15% is standard). Pack your bags tonight, set multiple alarms for tomorrow, and confirm your airport transfer. Keep your passport, flight documents, and any remaining colones easily accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early based on your flight time. Enjoy a final Costa Rican breakfast — gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, and a cup of excellent local coffee. Take one last walk on the beach or through the hotel garden. Spot any final wildlife — even the resort gardens often host hummingbirds, iguanas, and butterflies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is 11:00 AM — confirm with front desk). Arrange your pre-booked shared shuttle or bus to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for travel time and airport procedures. Use any remaining colones at the airport — there are shops and sodas inside where you can spend local currency.
day_by_day.evening: Clear security and immigration at the airport. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Costa Rican coffee or chocolate gifts. Board your flight home with incredible memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, zip-lining thrills, and pura vida living. Costa Rica will call you back — it always does.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto and Costa Rican coffee at the hotel — ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Airport soda or café — casado or sandwich — ~$7–10
meals.dinner: On the plane or airport restaurant depending on flight time

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip for departure: shared shuttles to the airport cost ~$15–25 per person vs $60–100 for private taxis. Book 24–48 hours in advance. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before international flights — Costa Rican immigration can have queues. Declare any agricultural products (coffee beans in sealed packages are fine; fresh fruit is not allowed). Keep your tourist tax receipt if you paid separately. Safe travels — pura vida!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to San José area hotel for overnight stay near airport.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit / airport food
meals.dinner: Light snack or grab-and-go from airport terminal before or after landing. Consider La Cantina inside the airport for a quick Costa Rican bite.

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule any activities tonight. Book an airport-adjacent hotel such as Hotel Aeropuerto or Wyndham San José Herradura for one night to avoid a long transfer after a late arrival. Confirm your transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort for the following day. Exchange some currency or withdraw colones at the airport ATM.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, check out of the airport hotel and arrange a private shuttle or rental car transfer toward your first destination. Head toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–3.5 hours from San José). Enjoy scenic views of the Central Valley and countryside as you travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in La Fortuna / Arenal area by early afternoon. Check into a mid-range lodge such as Hotel Magic Mountain or Arenal Manoa Resort. After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided walk around La Fortuna town, visit the La Fortuna Waterfall (La Catarata de La Fortuna) — a stunning 70-meter cascade reachable via a 30-minute hike down well-maintained steps.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the famous Tabacón or Baldi Hot Springs (mid-range entry fee around $40–60 USD) — thermal pools fed by volcanic activity with views of Arenal Volcano. A perfect way to unwind after travel.

meals.breakfast: Included at airport hotel or grab a 'gallo pinto' (rice and beans) breakfast at a local soda near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Stop en route at a roadside 'soda' (local diner) in Ciudad Quesada for a traditional casado (rice, beans, protein, salad) — budget $8–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Don Rufino in La Fortuna — a beloved mid-range restaurant serving Costa Rican cuisine with volcano views. Budget $20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: A 'soda' is a small, family-run Costa Rican restaurant offering affordable, authentic meals. La Fortuna Waterfall entrance fee is approximately $18 USD. Book hot springs in advance during peak season. Wear water shoes for the waterfall hike.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk — Join a guided morning tour through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges suspended up to 100 feet above the forest floor. Spot sloths, toucans, howler monkeys, and vibrant tree frogs in the misty jungle canopy. Tours typically depart at 7:30–8:00 AM for best wildlife activity. Duration: approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges tour, enjoy a kayaking or stand-up paddleboard session on Lake Arenal, one of Costa Rica's largest lakes with stunning volcano backdrops. Rentals available through local outfitters for $20–35 USD. Alternatively, visit the Arenal Natura Ecological Park for close-up encounters with caimans, frogs, snakes, and turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Explore La Fortuna's vibrant town center. Browse local artisan shops for handmade crafts and souvenirs. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the volcano.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Soda La Hormiga in La Fortuna for a classic Tico breakfast with fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lava Lounge Bar & Grill — casual outdoor setting with burgers, wraps, and local dishes. Budget $12–18 USD.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nene's — a local favorite for fresh fish, ceviche, and traditional Costa Rican dishes at very reasonable prices. Budget $15–22 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Hanging Bridges tour costs approximately $30–45 USD per person. Book through Arenal Hanging Bridges (Mistico Park) for a reputable experience. Morning tours offer the best wildlife sightings. Bring binoculars, sunscreen, and insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Sarapiquí or Toro River — a thrilling Class III–IV rapids experience through lush jungle gorges. Half-day tours depart around 8:00 AM from La Fortuna and include all equipment and a guide. Duration: approximately 3–4 hours on the water. This is a fantastic eco-adventure activity unique to the Arenal region.
day_by_day.afternoon: After rafting, freshen up at the lodge and visit the Arenal Volcano National Park hiking trails. Trek the Los Tucanes or Las Coladas trails through hardened lava fields with panoramic views of the volcano cone and surrounding rainforest. Entrance fee approximately $18 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Pack up and prepare for an early departure tomorrow. Enjoy a relaxed evening in La Fortuna. Optional: attend a cultural cooking class at a local restaurant to learn how to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto and arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the rafting tour — pack extra snacks for energy.
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch typically included with tour packages, or eat at Soda Viquez near the national park entrance for a hearty casado.
meals.dinner: El Novillo del Arenal — a steakhouse renowned for wood-fired meats and local river fish in an open-air setting. Budget $25–35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: White-water rafting tours cost approximately $65–90 USD per person and include transportation, equipment, and guides. Minimum age and weight restrictions may apply. Confirm booking 24 hours in advance. Keep valuables in waterproof bags.

day_by_day.morning: Depart La Fortuna early (7:00–8:00 AM) via the scenic Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer across Lake Arenal to Monteverde — a unique and iconic Costa Rican journey combining a 4WD vehicle, motorboat crossing, and another vehicle transfer. Arrive in Monteverde/Santa Elena by late morning (approximately 3 hours total). Check into a mid-range lodge such as Hotel Belmar or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, visit the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve for a self-guided afternoon walk. Explore misty trails through epiphyte-draped trees, spot resplendent quetzals (February is peak nesting season!), and observe the unique cloud forest microclimate. Entrance fee approximately $18 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming town of Santa Elena. Visit the Bat Jungle (an educational exhibit on bat ecology) or the Monteverde Cheese Factory for local artisan dairy products. Enjoy a leisurely evening stroll through the village.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast in La Fortuna before departure.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or stop at Café Colibri in Santa Elena upon arrival for sandwiches, fresh juices, and local pastries. Budget $10–15 USD.
meals.dinner: Tree House Restaurant & Café in Santa Elena — a beloved local institution built around a living fig tree, serving Costa Rican and international dishes. Budget $18–28 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer costs approximately $25–35 USD per person and is far more scenic and enjoyable than the long road route. Book in advance through your hotel or a local agency. February is an excellent time to spot resplendent quetzals in Monteverde — bring a good camera and binoculars.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits with Original Canopy Tour or Sky Adventures Monteverde. The circuit typically includes 10–15 platforms, Tarzan swings, and a rappel descent through the forest. Tours depart at 7:30 AM for the most atmospheric misty conditions. Duration: approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve — one of the most celebrated nature reserves in the world. Join a guided afternoon walk with a certified naturalist to spot golden toads (historically), three-wattled bellbirds, emerald toucanets, and countless orchid species. The reserve protects over 400 bird species and 100 mammal species.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest — a guided after-dark tour revealing the nocturnal world of the cloud forest. Spot kinkajous, sleeping birds, tarantulas, tree frogs, and glowing fungi with the help of expert guides and red-light flashlights. Duration: approximately 2 hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Stella's Bakery in Monteverde for fresh-baked goods, granola, and excellent local coffee.
meals.lunch: Soda La Esperanza near the reserve entrance — simple, filling casados and fresh fruit plates. Budget $8–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Café Flor de Vida — a vegetarian-friendly restaurant in Santa Elena offering creative Costa Rican fusion dishes using local organic ingredients. Budget $16–24 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line tour costs approximately $45–75 USD per person. Cloud forest reserve entrance is approximately $25 USD. Night walk tours cost approximately $25–35 USD per person. Book all three activities in advance as they fill up quickly on weekends. Wear layers — the cloud forest can be cool and misty, with temperatures dropping to 60–65°F (15–18°C).

day_by_day.morning: Morning birdwatching walk with a specialized ornithologist guide in the Monteverde area. February is peak season for spotting the iconic resplendent quetzal in its breeding plumage. Visit hummingbird galleries where dozens of species feed at close range — a photographer's paradise. Duration: approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Monteverde after lunch via private shuttle toward the Pacific Coast. Travel time to Manuel Antonio is approximately 4–5 hours. Enjoy the dramatic transition from cloud forest to coastal lowlands. Arrive at Aegean Bliss Resort in the Manuel Antonio / Quepos area by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and explore the beachfront property. Take a sunset walk along the beach, dip your toes in the Pacific Ocean, and decompress after several days of active adventure. Enjoy the resort's facilities — pool, bar, and ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Monteverde — fuel up before the transfer day.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Dominical or Quepos en route — try a local soda for fresh fish tacos or a seafood ceviche. Budget $10–15 USD.
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront restaurant — enjoy fresh Pacific seafood, tropical cocktails, and ocean breezes. Budget $25–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Private shuttle from Monteverde to Manuel Antonio costs approximately $55–80 USD per person. Alternatively, rent a car for more flexibility. Confirm your reservation at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure. The resort's beachfront location is ideal for the next several days of coastal exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio Wildlife Guided Rainforest Hike — Explore Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal hidden wildlife. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys (endemic to this region), iguanas, coatis, and vibrant poison dart frogs. Morning entry is essential as the park limits daily visitors. Park opens at 7:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, relax on the pristine white-sand beaches within Manuel Antonio National Park — Playa Manuel Antonio and Playa Espadilla Sur are among the most beautiful beaches in Costa Rica. Swim in the calm, clear Pacific waters and snorkel around the rocky headlands to spot colorful reef fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for sunset cocktails on the beachfront terrace. Enjoy the resort's amenities — spa treatments, pool, or hammock relaxation under palm trees.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the 7:00 AM park opening — pack water and snacks for the hike.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the beach inside the park, or eat at the park's casual café. Alternatively, El Avión Restaurant just outside the park — famous for its converted 1954 Fairchild C-123 cargo plane with Pacific views. Budget $18–28 USD.
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant at Gaia Hotel & Reserve — an upscale but accessible restaurant with creative Costa Rican cuisine and panoramic ocean views. Budget $30–45 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park entrance fee is approximately $20 USD per person. The park closes on Tuesdays, so Monday entry is ideal. Hire a certified guide at the park entrance for approximately $25–40 USD — they dramatically increase wildlife sightings. Bring biodegradable sunscreen, as chemical sunscreens are prohibited to protect the marine ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Since Manuel Antonio National Park is closed on Tuesdays, take a sea kayaking and snorkeling tour around the marine protected area near Manuel Antonio. Paddle through sea caves, spot dolphins, sea turtles, and tropical fish, and explore the coastline from the water. Tours depart from Quepos marina at 8:00 AM. Duration: approximately 4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jardín Gaia Wildlife Rescue Center — a sanctuary for rescued and rehabilitated wildlife including sloths, monkeys, toucans, and macaws. This educational experience provides close encounters with animals that cannot be released into the wild and supports important conservation work. Duration: approximately 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Quepos town — the charming fishing village adjacent to Manuel Antonio. Browse the weekly artisan market (if available), sample local street food, and experience authentic Costa Rican culture away from the tourist strip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — a leisurely morning meal before the kayaking departure.
meals.lunch: Barba Roja Restaurant on the Manuel Antonio road — a legendary open-air restaurant with fresh seafood, sushi, and Pacific views. Budget $18–28 USD.
meals.dinner: El Patio de Café Milagro in Quepos — a romantic restaurant known for creative fusion cuisine blending Costa Rican flavors with international techniques. Budget $22–35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sea kayaking and snorkeling tours cost approximately $65–85 USD per person and include equipment, guide, and snacks. Jardín Gaia entrance is approximately $20 USD. Tuesday is a great day to explore Quepos and surroundings since the national park is closed. Book kayaking tours in advance during peak February season.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide — Venture into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests (as declared by National Geographic) on a guided day hike. This requires an early departure from Manuel Antonio (5:30–6:00 AM) via boat or charter flight to Drake Bay or Sierpe, followed by a guided trek through primary rainforest teeming with tapirs, scarlet macaws, peccaries, and all four Costa Rican monkey species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado trek through the afternoon, exploring different habitat zones including beach, mangrove, and primary forest. Your naturalist guide will identify tracks, calls, and behaviors of elusive jungle wildlife. Swim at a pristine jungle beach during a rest stop.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to Manuel Antonio via boat/transfer, arriving back at Aegean Bliss Resort by 7:00–8:00 PM. This is a long but extraordinary day — one of the most rewarding wildlife experiences in all of Central America.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast at the resort before 5:30 AM departure — pack energy bars and trail mix.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator, eaten at a jungle rest stop or beach clearing inside the park.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the resort restaurant or a nearby delivery option — keep it simple after a long day. Alternatively, Santuario Restaurant at the resort for fresh local cuisine. Budget $20–30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado day trips from Manuel Antonio cost approximately $150–200 USD per person including transport, guide, park fees, and lunch. This is a premium experience but absolutely worth it for wildlife enthusiasts. The park requires a licensed guide — solo entry is not permitted. Wear sturdy hiking boots, long pants, and bring plenty of water. Book at least 1–2 weeks in advance as daily visitor numbers are strictly limited.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest and recovery morning after the Corcovado trek. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and relax at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront pool and spa. Optional: book a 60-minute therapeutic massage at the resort spa to soothe tired muscles from days of hiking and adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — While Tortuguero is geographically distant, Manuel Antonio area offers similar boat safari experiences through local mangrove waterways and estuaries. Book a local mangrove boat tour through Damas Island estuary (30 minutes from Manuel Antonio) — glide through the jungle waterways spotting howler monkeys, caimans, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, and countless bird species. Duration: approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the Pacific coastline from Quepos marina. Enjoy tropical cocktails, fresh ceviche, snorkeling stops, and spectacular sunset views over the Pacific Ocean. This is a quintessential Costa Rican coastal experience. Duration: approximately 3–4 hours.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort breakfast — treat yourself to the full spread including fresh tropical fruits, smoothies, and local pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort pool bar — ceviche, fish tacos, and fresh coconut water. Budget $15–20 USD.
meals.dinner: Catamaran cruise typically includes light snacks and drinks. Follow up with dinner at Agua Azul Restaurant — a cliffside eatery with spectacular ocean views and excellent fresh fish. Budget $22–35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Damas Island mangrove boat tour costs approximately $45–65 USD per person. Sunset catamaran cruise costs approximately $75–95 USD per person including drinks and snacks. Book both in advance. The mangrove tour is an excellent alternative to the full Tortuguero experience and is logistically much easier from Manuel Antonio.

day_by_day.morning: Waterfall rappelling and canyoning adventure in the Nauyaca Waterfalls area — one of the most spectacular natural attractions near Manuel Antonio. A guided horseback ride or hike (approximately 2 hours each way) through private farmland and rainforest leads to the stunning two-tiered Nauyaca Waterfalls (45m and 20m cascades). Swim in the natural pools beneath the falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the waterfall excursion and spend the afternoon at leisure on the beach. Rent a surfboard or bodyboard from the resort or local beach vendors and try the Pacific waves — Manuel Antonio's beaches offer manageable waves suitable for beginners. Alternatively, join a beginner surf lesson for approximately $40–60 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Manuel Antonio — celebrate the trip with a special dinner at one of the area's finest restaurants. Explore the local nightlife in Quepos if energy permits — the town has a lively bar scene with live music on Friday nights.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before the waterfall excursion departure (typically 7:00–7:30 AM).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at the base of Nauyaca Waterfalls — pack food from the resort or purchase a packed lunch from a local bakery the evening before.
meals.dinner: Kapi Kapi Restaurant — one of Manuel Antonio's most acclaimed fine-dining experiences featuring Costa Rican fusion cuisine with Asian influences, set in a stunning jungle-garden atmosphere. Budget $35–55 USD per person. Splurge-worthy for the final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Nauyaca Waterfalls guided tours cost approximately $65–90 USD per person including horseback riding or hiking, guide, and lunch. The round trip is approximately 4–5 hours. Wear water shoes and bring a dry bag for your camera. Book in advance — this is one of the most popular excursions in the area. The falls are most impressive in February due to recent rains.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — wake up early for one last sunrise walk along the beachfront. Take time to reflect on the incredible journey through cloud forests, volcanoes, rainforests, and coastlines. Optional: early morning yoga session on the beach (many resorts offer complimentary or low-cost sessions) or a final snorkeling session before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange private shuttle transfer back to San José / Juan Santamaría International Airport (approximately 3–3.5 hours). Stop en route at a local artisan market or souvenir shop to pick up last-minute gifts — look for locally produced coffee, chocolate, handmade jewelry, and traditional crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at San José airport with ample time for check-in and departure. If flight departs late evening, store luggage at the airport and explore the Multiplaza Escazú mall or the historic downtown San José briefly. Depart Costa Rica with unforgettable memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife, and natural wonders.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor fresh Costa Rican coffee, tropical fruits, and gallo pinto one last time.
meals.lunch: Stop en route to San José at Restaurante Tipico La Casona in Orotina or a roadside soda for a traditional farewell casado. Budget $10–15 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or pre-departure meal at Restaurante Nuestra Tierra near San José — a beloved institution serving traditional Costa Rican cuisine in a colorful, festive atmosphere. Budget $18–28 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in and security at Juan Santamaría Airport. Private shuttle from Manuel Antonio to San José airport costs approximately $55–80 USD per person or $120–180 USD for a private vehicle. Book in advance. Declare any agricultural products (coffee, fresh fruit) at customs. Costa Rica charges a departure tax that is typically included in modern airline tickets — confirm with your carrier.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do for eco-adventurers seeking an adrenaline rush above the treetops.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari spotting howler monkeys, caimans, river otters, toucans, and nesting sea turtles. This remote Caribbean-side park is one of Central America's most biodiverse wildlife corridors.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges suspended up to 100 feet above the forest floor, offering eye-level encounters with sloths, poison dart frogs, and exotic birds against the dramatic backdrop of Arenal Volcano.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio Wildlife Guided Rainforest Hike
experiences.description: Explore Manuel Antonio National Park with a certified naturalist guide who uses a high-powered spotting scope to reveal camouflaged sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, and rare birds hidden in the lush coastal rainforest, ending at a pristine white-sand beach.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a guided day hike through Corcovado, home to tapirs, scarlet macaws, white-lipped peccaries, and four species of monkeys. National Geographic called this 'the most biologically intense place on Earth.'

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a welcome cocktail and late-night snack prepared by the resort upon check-in. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity prepared by the resort – charcuterie board, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer through the resort concierge. Pack light in carry-on for easy access upon arrival. Request early turndown service and a morning wake-up call for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Take a private sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront property with a personal naturalist guide who introduces you to coastal birds and marine ecosystems of Costa Rica. Spot frigatebirds, brown pelicans, and sandpipers along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation session at the resort's eco-concierge desk to review your full itinerary and customize logistics. Spend the afternoon at the resort's infinity pool overlooking the Pacific, or enjoy a rejuvenating welcome spa treatment – choose from a volcanic mud wrap or a Costa Rican coffee body scrub at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cocktail hour on the resort terrace. Enjoy a curated dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced Costa Rican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant – freshly squeezed tropical juices, gallo pinto, eggs Benedict with smoked marlin, and artisanal Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – ceviche, fresh coconut, and grilled plantains with a tropical mocktail or craft beer
meals.dinner: Signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort – tasting menu featuring sea bass in hearts of palm sauce, Costa Rican wagyu beef, and a locally sourced dessert pairing with premium wine

day_by_day.notes: Use today as a recovery day from travel. Confirm all upcoming tour bookings with the concierge. Hydrate well – Costa Rica's humidity can be intense for new arrivals.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early via private luxury vehicle toward Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 20–30 minutes depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio Wildlife Guided Rainforest Hike with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs along the lush forest trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, enjoy exclusive beach time at Manuel Antonio's pristine Playa Biesanz or Playa Espadilla – one of the most beautiful beaches in Central America. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax on a private beach setup arranged by your guide. A packed premium picnic lunch will be served in a shaded beachside area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy a romantic dinner at a highly-rated local fine-dining restaurant near the resort, such as La Cantina or a comparable upscale establishment featuring fresh Pacific seafood.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure – açaí bowls, tropical fruit platters, and freshly brewed Costa Rican Tarrazú coffee
meals.lunch: Premium packed picnic at Manuel Antonio beach – artisan sandwiches, tropical fruit, local cheese, sparkling water, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Upscale local restaurant near the resort – whole grilled snapper, lobster bisque, and locally sourced desserts with a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored, lightweight clothing and closed-toe shoes for the hike. Apply reef-safe sunscreen. Bring binoculars for enhanced wildlife viewing. Manuel Antonio National Park has a daily visitor cap – ensure tickets are pre-booked through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to a nearby mangrove estuary or wetland reserve for a sunrise kayaking or paddleboarding experience through tranquil waterways. Spot crocodiles, caimans, roseate spoonbills, and river otters in their natural habitat with a private naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a leisurely afternoon. Enjoy a private cooking class with the resort's executive chef, learning to prepare traditional Costa Rican dishes including ceviche, patacones, and arroz con leche using locally sourced ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private beachfire dinner on the resort's beach – a bespoke dining experience set up by the resort team with tiki torches, a personal chef, and a curated menu under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure – granola, yogurt, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Post-kayak lunch at the resort's beach grill – grilled mahi-mahi tacos, fresh guacamole, and tropical agua fresca
meals.dinner: Private beachfire dinner – multi-course menu including grilled lobster tail, chimichurri steak, roasted vegetables, and a decadent chocolate lava cake with locally sourced cacao

day_by_day.notes: The private beachfire dinner must be arranged at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Confirm weather conditions for outdoor dining. Insect repellent recommended for evening activities.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure via private luxury vehicle or charter flight toward the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado National Park. Embark on the Corcovado National Park Day Trek with a certified naturalist guide – venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests. Encounter tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, giant anteaters, harpy eagles, and an extraordinary diversity of reptiles and amphibians.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided trek through Corcovado's primary rainforest trails, exploring pristine rivers and remote beaches within the park. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch in a stunning jungle clearing. Spot additional wildlife including scarlet macaws, toucans, and squirrel monkeys on the return trail.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (or overnight at a luxury eco-lodge near Corcovado if distance warrants – such as Lapa Rios Lodge or Bosque del Cabo). Enjoy a well-earned dinner and early rest after a full day of trekking.

meals.breakfast: Hearty early breakfast at the resort or lodge – scrambled eggs, fresh fruit, whole grain toast, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed jungle lunch – premium sandwiches, energy bars, tropical fruits, and filtered water provided by the guide service
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lapa Rios Lodge or equivalent luxury eco-lodge near Corcovado – farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine featuring local vegetables, sustainably caught fish, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado requires advance park permits – ensure these are secured through your concierge well in advance. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots and bring a rain jacket. Leech socks are recommended. This is the most physically demanding day of the trip – pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: If overnighting near Corcovado, enjoy a morning wildlife walk on the eco-lodge's private trails before transferring back to Aegean Bliss Resort. Alternatively, enjoy a morning dolphin-watching or whale-watching boat tour in the Golfo Dulce – a renowned marine biodiversity hotspot where spinner dolphins, bottlenose dolphins, and humpback whales are frequently sighted.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Spend a relaxing afternoon at the resort's wellness center – enjoy a traditional Temascal (pre-Columbian steam ceremony) or a deep tissue massage using locally sourced botanical oils.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the Pacific coastline, departing from a nearby marina. Enjoy cocktails, fresh ceviche, and live acoustic music as the sun dips below the horizon. Return to the resort for a quiet evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the eco-lodge or resort – tropical fruit, eggs to order, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at an acclaimed local restaurant near the marina – whole grilled fish, prawn skewers, and coconut rice
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort after the catamaran cruise – sushi-grade tuna tataki, roasted vegetables, and a glass of premium Malbec

day_by_day.notes: Confirm catamaran departure times and availability with the concierge. Bring a light jacket for the evening boat cruise as ocean breezes can be cool. Sunscreen and polarized sunglasses are essential for water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early via private charter flight or luxury vehicle toward Arenal Volcano area (approximately 3–4 hours by road or 1 hour by charter). Check in to a premium Arenal-area lodge such as Nayara Springs or The Springs Resort & Spa. Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk – trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspension bridges suspended up to 100 feet above the forest floor, with breathtaking views of Arenal Volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hanging bridges experience, spotting toucans, morpho butterflies, poison dart frogs, and howler monkeys in the canopy. After the walk, soak in natural volcanic hot springs at a premium private thermal pool facility exclusive to luxury guests.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the lodge's award-winning restaurant with a dramatic view of Arenal Volcano. Enjoy a curated menu featuring locally grown ingredients and premium Costa Rican craft spirits.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure or en route at a highly-rated café – gallo pinto, fresh eggs, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the hanging bridges visitor center's premium dining area or a nearby upscale restaurant – rainforest-inspired cuisine with fresh local produce
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Nayara Springs or The Springs Resort restaurant – multi-course tasting menu with Arenal Volcano views, featuring locally sourced beef, fresh river fish, and artisanal Costa Rican chocolate desserts

day_by_day.notes: A charter flight to Arenal (La Fortuna Airport) is strongly recommended to maximize time. Book the private thermal pool session in advance. The hanging bridges walk is moderate in difficulty – wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a guided birdwatching tour around Lake Arenal and the surrounding wetlands. Spot resplendent quetzals (seasonal), montane solitary eagles, and over 100 species of birds endemic to the Arenal region with a specialist ornithologist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water rafting on the Balsa or Toro River (Class III–IV rapids) with a premium adventure outfitter – an exhilarating half-day experience through lush jungle gorges with expert guides and top-of-the-line safety equipment. Alternatively, opt for a guided kayaking tour on Lake Arenal for a more serene experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a private couples' or solo spa treatment at the lodge's volcanic spa – featuring hot stone massage with basalt stones and volcanic mud facials. Enjoy a nightcap at the lodge's volcano-view bar.

meals.breakfast: Early birdwatching breakfast box provided by the lodge – fresh fruit, granola bars, hard-boiled eggs, and thermos of coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch at a premium riverside restaurant – Costa Rican casado (rice, beans, plantains, and protein), fresh fruit agua fresca
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining at the lodge – customized three-course menu prepared by a personal chef, served on your private terrace with volcano views

day_by_day.notes: Confirm river conditions and rafting class with the outfitter before departure. Bring a change of dry clothes for after the rafting experience. The birdwatching tour is best conducted between 5:30–8:00 AM when bird activity peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal area via private charter flight or luxury vehicle toward Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve. Check in to a premium Monteverde lodge such as El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Monteverde Lodge & Gardens. Begin an early afternoon orientation walk through the lodge's private cloud forest trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the flagship experience of the trip – the Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour. Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic and thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring multiple lines, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges at exhilarating heights above the forest floor. Experience the magic of the cloud forest from a bird's-eye perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk through Monteverde Cloud Forest with a specialist naturalist guide to spot nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, sleeping birds, glass frogs, and tarantulas. Return to the lodge for a warm dinner by the fireplace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure – eggs, fresh fruit, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Monteverde restaurant upon arrival – cloud forest-inspired cuisine featuring local cheese, hearts of palm salad, and wood-fired meats
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Silencio Lodge or equivalent – hearty mountain cuisine featuring local trout, organic vegetables from the lodge's garden, and warm chocolate fondant with cloud forest honey

day_by_day.notes: Monteverde is significantly cooler than coastal areas – pack a light fleece or jacket. The zip-line tour typically has weight restrictions (check in advance). The night walk requires closed-toe shoes and a headlamp (provided by the guide).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Children's Eternal Rainforest (Bosque Eterno de los Niños) – the largest private nature reserve in Central America. Walk through pristine cloud forest with a specialist guide, spotting resplendent quetzals, three-wattled bellbirds, and emerald toucanets. Visit the Hummingbird Gallery where dozens of species feed at close range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería) – a historic cooperative that produces artisanal cheeses using traditional Dutch methods. Enjoy a premium guided tasting of local cheeses, followed by a visit to a local coffee and chocolate farm for an immersive tasting experience of Costa Rica's finest agricultural products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the lodge for a private chef's table dinner – an intimate, multi-course experience with the lodge's head chef who presents a curated menu inspired by cloud forest ingredients, paired with premium Costa Rican craft wines and spirits.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast – cloud forest granola, local eggs, fresh-baked bread, and Monteverde artisanal coffee
meals.lunch: Artisanal cheese, charcuterie, and local produce tasting at the Monteverde Cheese Factory – paired with local craft beer or wine
meals.dinner: Private chef's table at the lodge – six-course tasting menu with cloud forest-inspired flavors, wine pairing, and a personalized dessert creation

day_by_day.notes: Book the private chef's table experience in advance through the lodge. The Children's Eternal Rainforest requires advance permits – coordinate through your concierge. Quetzal sightings are most likely in early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde via private luxury vehicle toward Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (approximately 4–5 hours, including a boat transfer through the canals). Alternatively, take a charter flight to Tortuguero airstrip for maximum efficiency. Check in to a premium Tortuguero lodge such as Tortuga Lodge & Gardens or Manatus Hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a private guided boat safari, spotting howler monkeys, caimans, river otters, manatees, green herons, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds along the canal banks. The afternoon light is perfect for wildlife photography.
day_by_day.evening: If visiting during sea turtle nesting season (February may see early green turtles), join an exclusive guided beach walk to observe nesting sea turtles under the supervision of certified wildlife monitors. Return to the lodge for a riverside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure – light and energizing with fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch en route or at the Tortuguero lodge upon arrival – Caribbean-style cuisine featuring rice and beans cooked in coconut milk, fried plantains, and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tortuga Lodge or Manatus Hotel – Caribbean fusion menu featuring jerk-spiced chicken, coconut curry shrimp, and tropical fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small aircraft – no roads lead to the village. Pack light for the boat transfer. Sea turtle nesting schedules vary – confirm with the lodge naturalist upon arrival. Bring rain gear as the Caribbean coast receives significant rainfall year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private boat tour through the secondary canals of Tortuguero National Park – explore narrower waterways inaccessible to larger boats for an intimate wildlife encounter. Spot Jesus Christ lizards, poison dart frogs, three-toed sloths, and dozens of bird species including the keel-billed toucan and great green macaw.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy Research Station for a behind-the-scenes educational tour on sea turtle conservation efforts in Tortuguero. Participate in a volunteer data recording session if available. Spend the remainder of the afternoon relaxing at the lodge's riverside pool or enjoying a therapeutic massage at the lodge spa.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Caribbean dinner at the lodge – a special multi-course meal celebrating the penultimate evening of your Costa Rican adventure. Toast with premium rum cocktails made with locally produced Guaro and tropical fruits.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the morning boat tour – fresh fruit, granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge – Caribbean lobster salad, coconut rice, and freshly pressed tropical juices
meals.dinner: Special farewell Caribbean dinner at the lodge – whole grilled snook, Caribbean rice and beans, roasted plantains, and a decadent tres leches cake with local vanilla

day_by_day.notes: Photography is outstanding in Tortuguero's narrow canals – bring a waterproof camera bag. The Sea Turtle Conservancy visit may require advance reservation. Confirm return transfer logistics to San José for Day 13 with the lodge concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise boat ride through the Tortuguero canals – a quiet, reflective farewell to the waterways and wildlife that have defined this extraordinary journey. Return to the lodge for a leisurely final breakfast. Pack and prepare for departure via private boat transfer and onward to San José.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in San José with time for last-minute premium souvenir shopping at Galería Namu (authentic indigenous art) or the Mercado Central for artisanal Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and handcrafted goods. If time permits, enjoy a brief guided cultural tour of San José's historic Teatro Nacional (National Theater) – a stunning 19th-century architectural gem.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-flight farewell dinner at one of San José's finest restaurants – Sikwa (indigenous Costa Rican tasting menu), Nueve (modern Costa Rican cuisine), or Park Café (European-Costa Rican fusion). Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport for your departure flight with premium private airport transfer.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge – eggs benedict, fresh tropical fruits, Costa Rican coffee, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch in San José at a premium café – artisanal sandwiches, fresh salads, and locally sourced juices
meals.dinner: Farewell fine-dining dinner in San José – tasting menu at Sikwa or Nueve featuring the best of Costa Rican gastronomy, paired with premium wines and ending with a signature Costa Rican cacao dessert

day_by_day.notes: Depart Tortuguero early enough to allow 3–4 hours in San José before your flight. Confirm departure flight details and arrange private airport transfer in advance. Allow extra time at the airport for international departure – arrive at least 3 hours before your flight. Pack any purchased coffee or chocolate in checked luggage to avoid customs issues.
